- [In patients with biopsy grade group 2 – 4 undergoing radical prostatectomy, mm of pattern 4 on biopsy better predictor of advanced surgical pathology and biochemical recurrence than either grade group or a multivariable model of standard clinical predictors](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41867176/){target="_blank"}<br><span style="font-size:0.95em;">Pickersgill NA, Fletcher SA, Aiken N, Assel MJ, Liso N, Reuter VE, Vickers AJ, Ehdaie B, Fine SW. - [Patients with grade group 2 – 4 with <2mm of pattern 4 on biopsy have equivalent risk to those in the favorable intermediate risk category - and hence are eligible for active surveillance – but constitute a group that is twice as large](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42830647/){target="_blank"}<br><span style="font-size:0.95em;">Fletcher SA, Pickersgill NA, Aiken N, Assel MJ, Liso N, Reuter VE, Ehdaie B, Fine SW, Vickers AJ. ### Findings best explained by pattern 4 volume being prognostic

- [Tumor volume assessed on MRI predicts 7-year risk of metastasis after surgery or radiotherapy (MRI volume reflects amount of pattern 4)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39470422/){target="_blank"}
  <br><span style="font-size:0.95em;">Yang DD, Lee LK, Tsui JMG, Leeman JE, McClure HM, Sudhyadhom A, Guthier CV, Taplin ME, Trinh QD, Mouw KW, Martin NE, Orio PF, Nguyen PL, D'Amico AV, Shin KY, Lee KN, King MT. AI-derived Tumor Volume from Multiparametric MRI and Outcomes in Localized Prostate Cancer. Radiology. 2024 Oct;313(1):e240041. doi: 10.1148/radiol.240041. PMID: 39470422.</span>
  
-	Numerous papers have found if grade is discordant between settings (e.g. targeted and systematic biopsy, or between biopsy and surgical pathology), risk is intermediate between the two grades. This is best explained in terms of pattern 4 volume. The larger the tumor (and hence for a given Gleason score, the larger the amount of pattern 4), the more likely sampling will be adequate and the less likely it is to find discordant Gleason scores
